title: Rollback Advisor: staged apply + cost-aware guardrails and state reconciler
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Build an automated Rollback Advisor service that will safely apply configuration changes (batching, cache policies, quantization/profiles and routing) and automatically reconcile state when regressions or unsafe runs are detected. The advisor will combine cost signals (tokens/unit cost, KV cache miss rate, batching efficiency), correctness/quality signals (eval regressions, hallucination rate proxies), and reliability signals (error rate, tail latency) to trigger guardrails and rollbacks. This ticket covers the design and MVP implementation for staged applies (canary -> ramp -> global), explicit guardrail rules, anomaly detectors, and a state reconciler that ensures eventual consistency between desired config and cluster state after intermittent failures.
acceptance_criteria: Canary applies execute to a 1% traffic slice with isolated metrics and log grouping
Automated rollback triggers exist for: >20% token cost increase, >15% cache miss rate regression, >2x p99 latency, >3% error rate, failed quality evals
State reconciler can detect drift and reapply desired config within configured backoff windows
Rollback actions are auditable in Console with links to PRs, diffs, and incident notes
Dry-run simulation mode produces delta report and policy violations without mutating production state
Unit and e2e tests for rollback logic and reconciler exist and pass in CI
tasks: Design API + policy DSL for guardrails (risk thresholds, hysteresis, scoped exceptions)
Implement canary routing plumbing and metrics isolation in serving runtime
Build anomaly detector pipeline for cost and cache signals (Prometheus -> alert rules)
Implement rollback orchestration workflow (revert, patch, or traffic-redirect)
State reconciler: implement compare-and-apply loop with exponential backoff and audit log
Console UI: expose advisor decisions, allow manual override and approval flow
Security review and KMS/HSM handling for private deployments
Create simulated workloads and integration tests for batching/caching recommendation regressions
Prepare runbook and incident playbook for false-positive rollbacks
notes: Background: Multiple customers reported sudden token-cost spikes after applying batching changes. Root cause often a misconfigured prefix cache TTL or an aggressive batch size that pushes requests into slow kernels, increasing p99 latency and cost. We need automated, reversible applies that reason about cost and correctness together.

Scope: MVP focuses on config changes that impact runtime execution (batch size, batch timeout, cache TTL/policy, recommended quantization profile). We intentionally exclude large model swaps and infra-level changes in MVP.

Guardrail philosophy: Prefer safe defaults + explicit opt-in for aggressive cost savings. Use hysteresis windows to avoid flip-flopping during transient noise. Every automated rollback must include cause metadata and a recommended manual action.

Reconciler details: Compare desired state (Config DB / Git-backed specs) with observed state (agent reported active config). On mismatch, attempt up to N retries with backoff. If reconciliation fails due to conflict with another change, notify on-call and create an incident ticket.

Signals we will use: token_rate, token_cost_per_minute, KV_cache_hit_rate, batch_utilization, p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate, eval_quality_score, anomalous_output_rate (heuristic), infra_cpu/gpu_saturation.

Rollback actions considered: immediate revert to prior config, gradual traffic reweight to fallback model, throttle new applies (pause pipeline), or apply compensating configuration (reduce batch size, increase cache TTL).
Observability: All advisor decisions must emit structured events to event-stream (kafka) and appear in Console under a new 'Advisor' timeline with links to metrics queries and PR diffs.

Design trade-offs: Automated rollbacks reduce blast radius but can hide root-cause if too aggressive. We will implement a 'soft rollback' mode for initial deployment that requires two independent detectors to trigger before automated revert.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy DSL parsing and evaluation
Integration tests for canary routing and metrics isolation using localbench harness
Chaos test: introduce synthetic KV cache miss spike and validate rollback path triggers
E2E: simulate a batching recommendation apply (increase batch size) and measure cost/latency impact; verify advisor rolls back on defined thresholds
Manual QA: product review of Console UX and audit flows
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positive rollbacks causing unnecessary churn. Mitigation: soft-rollback mode + multi-signal confirmation + cooldown windows
Risk: Reconciler thrashing with concurrent deploys. Mitigation: global operation locks and conflict detection; escalate to on-call instead of indefinite retries

Risk: Overly permissive guardrails preventing beneficial cost optimizations. Mitigation: add operator overrides and an 'optimization lab' sandbox where recommendations are validated before production rollout
Risk: Security exposure in private deployments when advisor needs to read configs. Mitigation: read-only query patterns, KMS for any secret access, and security review
milestones: M1: API + policy DSL spec complete (2025-11-18)
M2: Canary plumbing + metric isolation implemented (2025-11-22)
M3: Anomaly detectors + rollback orchestration MVP (2025-11-26)
M5: Security review and full e2e tests (2025-12-05)
